$comment: The policy archive: federal label requirements as versioned data. Extracted from the eCFR versioner API, digests included so a later re-extraction can detect that a regulation moved. Rules are superseded, never deleted (D27); nothing is enforced without a named approval. Design: design.md §18.

source.$comment: Numeric lists are parsed from the fetched text, never transcribed.

$dating: TWO DIFFERENT DATES, deliberately kept apart. `effectiveFrom` on a rule is the range of SUBMISSION dates it governs — an application filed in 2024 must be judged by the rules in force in 2024, not today's. `extractedFromIssueDate` on a regulation is when this deployment last read the text. Conflating them would let a rule change silently re-judge past decisions.

regulations.heading: Class and type designation (Beverage Alcohol Manual, distilled spirits)
regulations.textDigest: pages 1-6 and 9-12 read; not fingerprinted (PDF, not eCFR XML)
regulations.$comment: TTB's own guidance restating the standards of identity in 27 CFR 5 subpart C. Cited as the practical source; the binding text is the CFR.

coverage.$comment: Stated so silence is never read as compliance.
coverage.Distilled spirits: mandatory information, alcohol content, standards of fill; class/type minimum bottling strength extracted as a DRAFT from BAM ch. 4 (pages 1-6, 9-12 of 30 read)
coverage.Malt beverages: not extracted — part 7 read for section titles only. A rule set that half-covers a commodity is worse than one that says it does not.

rules.requirement: The brand name appears on the label.
The class, type, or other designation appears on the label.
Alcohol content is stated as a percentage of alcohol by volume.
Net contents appear on the container.
rules.$note: Absence from artwork is NOT a breach: 5.63(b)(2) permits net contents to be blown, embossed or moulded into the container, which no label image can show. Absent therefore means UNDETERMINED and goes to the agent.

rules.requirement: The statement reads "Alcohol __ percent by volume", "__ percent alcohol by volume", or "Alcohol by volume __ percent"; alcohol may be "alc", percent may be "%", "by" may be "/", volume may be "vol", periods and parentheses optional.
Where degrees of proof are also stated, proof is twice the alcohol by volume.
rules.$note: Answers open question Q8. Needs no application data and no model — the label is checked against itself.

rules.requirement: Net contents are an authorised metric standard of fill for distilled spirits.
rules.$note: Amended by T.D. TTB-200, 90 FR 1876 (10 Jan 2025), which changed the authorised list. The prior list is NOT in this archive, so a submission filed before that date is UNDETERMINED for this rule rather than judged by a list that did not govern it.

rules.requirement: Net contents are an authorised standard of fill for wine.
rules.$note: 4.72(b) permits containers above 3 litres in even litres; this rule stops at 3 litres and a larger container is NOT_APPLICABLE, not a breach.

rules.requirement: The health warning statement appears word for word as prescribed.
rules.$note: Implemented before this archive existed, against config/warning-statement.json. Listed so the set describes everything checked, not only what it added.

rules.requirement: The stated alcohol content is not below the minimum bottling strength for the labelled class or type.

provenance.quote: Spirits distilled from a fermented mash of grain at less than 95% alcohol by volume (190 proof) ... and bottled at not less than 40% alcohol by volume (80 proof)

rules.$note: DRAFT, not active. Extracted by a model from a supplied PDF and not yet approved by a person — which is the contract working as intended rather than an oversight. It also needs the class/type vocabulary problem below resolved first.
rules.$openQuestion: The table is keyed by class name, but a label states a DESIGNATION ('Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey') which must be resolved to its class ('Whisky') before the bound applies. That resolution is a taxonomy lookup this system does not have. Note also the spelling: the BAM writes 'Whisky', the corpus label reads 'Whiskey', and both are permitted — a naive set membership test would produce a confident false finding on a compliant label.
